pr_title: Updating compileTemplate to use `id` instead of `compilerOptions.scopeId`
pr_body:
Closes #5629 

Vue have changed their API to require the `id` field instead of `compilerOptions.scopeId`. They also remove the `data-v-` prefix.

issue_context.title: Vue warning: compileTemplate now requires the `id` option.
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

There's a warning when running the integration tests (and probably also when actually using the Vue transformer in a project):

```
[@vue/compiler-sfc] compileTemplate now requires the `id` option.`.
```

## Possible solution

Looking at 
https://github.com/vuejs/vue-next/blob/13fc8ff9dd7007e4ef7d2f0b6e5c973013ccc8b8/packages/compiler-sfc/src/compileTemplate.ts#L189-L212

I would say this should instead use `id` and not `compilerOptions.shortId`?
https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/6e81ebff219f13e2049638923b8819f0a63d40be/packages/transformers/vue/src/VueTransformer.js#L252-L254

But I don't actually know what `id` does...

cc @101arrowz
comments:
Vue has a feature called scoped CSS that is like CSS modules but easier to use. To make it work, it applies styles to elements that match your provided selector AND have the scope ID as a `data-` attribute. Basically, each element gets a `data-v-abcdef` attribute and scoped CSS targets `.your-selector[data-v-abcdef] { ... }`.

Vue must have changed their API to require the `id` field instead of `scopeId`. Trivial to change: replace `scopeId` with `id`. Optionally remove the `data-v` prefix, since it's removed by Vue anyway.
I'm happy to do this if that's ok?

review_comments: You may consider removing this/renaming variables for clarity
I considered that but I thought that keeping `scopeId` provided more clarity than just `id`, and kept changes minimal.
